posts.name: avienn_a
posts.cooked:
Key Takeaways

The MCP Server is now built into Studio with no additional setup required. Assistant can start and stop playtests and simulate player input, enabling an end-to-end loop where it can reproduce issues, validate fixes, and iterate autonomously. Plus, we’ve streamlined the script approval flow.

We’re back with another round of updates designed to make AI-assisted development in Studio more powerful and easier to use. Here’s what’s new.

Studio Built-in MCP Server

We’re bringing the MCP Server natively into Studio. If you’ve been using our open source MCP server, the built-in server is now the recommended way to connect external AI tools to Studio. Tools will be in sync with Assistant automatically, so you’ll always have the latest capabilities without pulling updates manually. The OSS server will remain available for those who want to contribute or customize.

For step-by-step instructions on enabling the MCP Server in Studio and connecting it to popular clients like Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Visual Studio Code, Cursor, and Antigravity, see the Studio MCP Server Documentation and Setup Guide.

image (37)1214×872 107 KB

Manage your MCP Servers by selecting the “…” within the Assistant widget

Key updates in this version include:

  • Full tool parity with Assistant: Every MCP tool available in Assistant is automatically available through the built-in MCP Server. As we add new capabilities to Assistant, they’ll be reflected in the MCP Server in lockstep, with no manual syncing or version mismatches.
  • Connect to multiple Studio instances: You can now connect a single MCP client to multiple running instances of Studio simultaneously through two new tools:
    • list_roblox_studios: Lists all connected Roblox Studio instances so you can identify which one to work with
    • set_active_studio: Sets a specific Studio instance as active (all subsequent tool calls will go to that instance until changed)
    • The MCP Server will infer which Studio instance you’re referring to based on the context of your request, whether you mention a specific game by name or reference something that only exists in one of your connected experiences. This feature is still experimental — see the FAQ below for tips on working with multiple Studio instances. Let us know any feedback you have.

Playtest Automation with Virtual Input

We are adding full playtest automation with virtual input support. Assistant and Studio’s built-in MCP Server can now programmatically start and stop play sessions and simulate player input directly within those sessions at your command.

This means Assistant can do more than just write and modify code. It can interact with your experience the way a player would. When asked, Assistant can click buttons, press keys, navigate menus, move characters, and validate that gameplay works correctly, all without you needing to manually test each change. This creates a true end-to-end development loop: plan, execute, and test using AI with minimal manual intervention.

This update includes the following new tools, which can be enabled/disabled from the Assistant UI:

  • start_stop_play: Start and stop a playtest session and capture debug output
  • get_console_output: Reads the output logs within a playtest session
  • user_mouse_input: Simulates real mouse clicks and movements, enabling Assistant to take actions in the game like clicking through a UI
  • user_keyboard_input: Simulates real keyboard presses, enabling Assistant to complete actions that require the keyboard like walking or jumping
  • character_navigation: Moves a character directly to a position or instance in the place, handling pathfinding automatically. Unlike the tools above, this does not simulate real player input. It bypasses the input system to move the character directly.

image1996×524 41.9 KB

Access first party tools settings by clicking the slider icon within Assistant input window

Here are a few example use cases:

  • End-to-end UI testing: When enabled, Assistant can open your experience, click through menu flows, and verify that each screen behaves correctly

  • Gameplay validation: After modifying a gameplay script, Assistant can start a playtest, simulate player input, and iterate to confirm the changes work as intended

  • Automated regression checks: Combine virtual input with console output reading to catch issues before they ship

Other improvements

  • We’ve improved how Assistant handles script change approvals. You can now accept all script edits on a per-session or per-prompt basis
    • This allows Assistant to apply changes, run verification loops, and iterate on implementations continuously, even while you step away
    • When you come back, you’ll find tested, validated changes ready for your review. This is a small but meaningful quality-of-life improvement that removes friction from longer, multi-step workflows
  • We’re continuously improving the Roblox Default model to enhance overall performance and reliability. These ongoing updates focus on refining core functionality and ensuring a more consistent experience as we iterate based on user feedback and usage patterns!

What’s next

As mentioned in our last post, we’ll be rolling out regular improvements to both Assistant and our MCP server in the coming months so stay tuned to find out more. Please let us know if you run into any issues or have suggestions for new features you’d find useful.

Happy creating!

The Roblox Studio Team

FAQs

Click here to view

Can I connect to multiple Studio instances at the same time?

  • Yes! This was one of the most requested features from the community. A single MCP client can now connect to multiple running Studio instances, and the server will try to infer which instance you’re referring to based on context. You can also switch manually using the list_roblox_studios and set_active_studio tools. This is still experimental, so let us know how it works for you.

What’s the difference between the built-in MCP Server and the open source one?

  • The built-in MCP Server is now the recommended option. It lives natively in Studio and stays in sync with Assistant automatically, so you always have the latest tools without pulling updates. The OSS server will remain available for those who want to contribute or customize.

Does playtest automation actually play my game like a real player?

  • The mouse, keyboard, and UI input tools simulate real player input. The one exception is character_navigation, which bypasses the input system and moves the character directly using pathfinding.

Can Assistant test my game while I’m away?

  • Yes. With the new per-session or per-prompt auto-accept for script edits, Assistant can apply changes, run playtests, and iterate without waiting for manual approval on each step. You can review the results when you’re back.

Where can I find setup instructions?

  • See the Studio MCP Server Documentation and Setup Guide linked here for step-by-step instructions on connecting to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, VS Code, Cursor, and Antigravity.

posts.name: Perthyz
posts.cooked:
Hey, this is a great addition! It really lowers the barrier to entry for game development. An imaginative kid can now turn ideas from their daydreams into actual conceptualized games.

I’m really excited to see what Roblox comes up with next. That said, I don’t think this necessarily provides the capability to create a fully fledged complex game. Traditional programming, playtesting, modeling, etc, will always remain core pillars of game development. AI mainly helps lower the time required to reach a minimum viable product.

I also don’t think AI should be entirely relied on for full automation of game development. In my opinion, there should be a human in between each step of the product.

Perthyz:

I also don’t think AI should be entirely relied on for full automation of game development. In my opinion, there should be a human in between each step of the product.

These tools are specifically meant for the LLM to iterate on it’s own output before presenting it to you. You are still going to be there for every step, the automated playtesting just reduces the headache and amount of steps you need to take to get quality output.
